question: Why do some pregnant women in Nigerian communities hide their traditional practices from healthcare workers?

options.A: Strict government laws banning all local birth customs
options.B: High cost of purchasing traditional herbal remedies
options.C: Lack of available transport to local health facilities
options.D: Fear of being dismissed or judged by orthodox providers

explanation: When health workers dismiss local customs, patients keep secrets to avoid harsh criticism. [learn more](BMP215_U3_T3#BMP215_U3_T3_h1)

question: Why must midwives understand the cultural background of pregnant women in their communities?

options.A: To document every local superstition for government research
options.B: To replace all modern medical care with local herbal treatments
options.C: To ensure patients follow strict international hospital rules
options.D: To build trust and encourage women to attend antenatal clinics

explanation: A good working relationship built on mutual respect keeps mothers coming back for safe professional care. [learn more](BMP215_U3_T3#BMP215_U3_T3_h1)

question: Which traditional method used to speed up labor can cause a uterine rupture?

options.A: Massaging the soles of the feet with warm palm oil
options.B: Encouraging the mother to walk around the room
options.C: Applying heavy downward force on the upper abdomen
options.D: Offering sips of clean water during early contractions

explanation: Fundal pressure puts extreme stress on the uterine muscle and can tear it open during labor. [learn more](BMP215_U3_T3#BMP215_U3_T3_h2)

question: What is the main danger of dietary taboos that restrict meat and eggs during pregnancy?

options.A: They contribute to maternal nutritional deficiencies and anemia
options.B: They lower the mother's blood sugar to fatal levels instantly
options.C: They immediately trigger premature rupture of the membranes
options.D: They cause the unborn baby to grow dangerously large in size

explanation: Restricting protein foods deprives the mother of essential nutrients needed for blood production and fetal growth. [learn more](BMP215_U3_T3#BMP215_U3_T3_h2)

question: Which of these is an example of a beneficial traditional practice during childbirth?

options.A: Fasting completely from food and water throughout active labor
options.B: Drinking concentrated herbal tonics to dilate the cervix quickly
options.C: Applying caustic substances to the newborn's umbilical cord stump
options.D: Having a trusted female family member present for emotional support

explanation: Continuous support from a familiar companion lowers anxiety and improves overall birth outcomes. [learn more](BMP215_U3_T3#BMP215_U3_T3_h3)

question: A new mother wants to rest warmly and eat traditional nourishing broths after delivery. How should the midwife respond?

options.A: Encourage the practice while ensuring she also drinks enough clean water and eats balanced meals
options.B: Warn her that local broths contain toxins that will interfere with successful breastfeeding
options.C: Demand she stop eating traditional foods immediately in favor of standard hospital meals
options.D: Ignore her dietary choices completely as they have no impact on her physical recovery

explanation: Warm rest and nourishing broths support recovery, provided overall nutrition and hydration remain adequate. [learn more](BMP215_U3_T3#BMP215_U3_T3_h3)

question: What is the most effective approach for a midwife trying to stop a harmful traditional practice?

options.A: Shaming the mother in front of other patients to teach a lesson
options.B: Threatening the family with police arrest if they disobey medical advice
options.C: Using patient education and offering safe, acceptable alternatives
options.D: Ignoring the dangerous practice entirely to avoid causing any argument

explanation: Education combined with practical alternatives works best because it addresses the root reason behind the custom. [learn more](BMP215_U3_T3#BMP215_U3_T3_h4)

question: Why do direct insults and aggressive lectures usually fail when addressing harmful birth practices?

options.A: They make families defensive and drive them away from health facilities
options.B: They automatically increase the physical strength of the harmful herbs
options.C: They violate international laws regarding traditional medicine use
options.D: They prevent community leaders from attending future hospital meetings

explanation: Aggressive criticism alienates patients, causing them to seek care from hidden, unsafe sources. [learn more](BMP215_U3_T3#BMP215_U3_T3_h4)

question: What is the primary role assigned to Traditional Birth Attendants in collaborative maternal health programs?

options.A: Prescribing pharmaceutical antibiotics for severe maternal infections
options.B: Recognizing pregnancy danger signs and referring complications early
options.C: Replacing licensed midwives at all rural primary health clinics
options.D: Performing major surgical operations during complicated deliveries

explanation: Training TBAs to spot warning signs ensures high-risk mothers reach skilled care without dangerous delays. [learn more](BMP215_U3_T3#BMP215_U3_T3_h5)

question: Why is building a working relationship with TBAs important in rural Nigerian settings?

options.A: Government policy requires TBAs to take over all hospital maternity wards
options.B: Local women refuse to speak with orthodox midwives under any circumstances
options.C: TBAs have advanced scientific training in managing severe obstetric bleeding
options.D: TBAs are often trusted first responders in communities with limited health access

explanation: Because many women consult TBAs first, partnering with them is vital for timely emergency referrals. [learn more](BMP215_U3_T3#BMP215_U3_T3_h5)
